0.name: Land
0.rule: At least 4 of the hex's 7 sample points (the centre and 6 more) fall in a SIANE municipality or a Natural Earth country, unless the centre is sea and the ETOPO1 mean is at or below sea level, or at least half its ETOPO1 samples are (rías and estuaries stay water).

1.name: Ocean
1.rule: Sea deeper than 200 m and not next to land.

2.name: Coast
2.rule: Sea next to a land hex, or shallower than 200 m (ETOPO1 mean).

3.name: Lake
3.rule: Water hex (most of its 7 sample points off land) with more Natural Earth 1:10m lake points than sea points, or above sea level.

0.name: Flat
0.rule: Elevation standard deviation inside the hex under 32 m.

1.name: Hills
1.rule: Elevation standard deviation of 32 m or more.

2.name: Mountains
2.rule: Elevation standard deviation of 138 m or more, or mean elevation of 2,300 m or more.

3.name: Peaks
3.rule: Mean elevation of 2,700 m or more (high mountains).

0.name: None
0.rule: Water, foreign land, or no CORINE land pixels.

1.name: Broadleaved forest
1.rule: Forest (NLCD 41+42+43) is the largest group and broadleaved (41) its largest type.

2.name: Conifer forest
2.rule: Forest is the largest group and evergreen (42) its largest type.

3.name: Mixed forest
3.rule: Forest is the largest group and mixed (43) its largest type.

4.name: Scrub & desert
4.rule: Scrub (52) is the largest group: maquis, garrigue, heathland and semi-arid land.

5.name: Grassland
5.rule: Grassland (71) plus urban open space (21: parks, sports grounds) is the largest group.

6.name: Pasture
6.rule: Meadows and pasture (81) are the largest group.

8.name: Wetland
8.rule: Woody (90) and herbaceous (95) wetlands together are the largest group.

9.name: Urban
9.rule: Built-up land of low, medium or high intensity (22+23+24) covers 30% or more of the hex's land, whatever else is there.

10.name: Barren
10.rule: Bare ground (31: rock, sand, salt pans) is the largest group.

11.name: Ice & snow
11.rule: Perennial ice and snow (12) are the largest group.

notes.water: The SIANE 1:3M municipal boundaries and the Natural Earth 1:10m country and lake outlines do not fit exactly. A sea hex whose ETOPO1 mean is above sea level (with fewer than half its samples below it) becomes land if at least 4 of its 6 neighbours are land, or if it touches both Spanish and foreign land; it takes the owner most of its neighbours have. A sea hex's elevation is the mean of its ETOPO1 samples below sea level (its depth). The Canary Islands are drawn in a box south-west of the peninsula; their hexes keep their real elevation and land cover.
notes.relief: From the ETOPO1 samples (1 arc-minute, about 1.85 km apart, some 25 per 10 km hex) at -100 m or higher, so that bays and sea floor do not count; if none is, all are used. Water hexes are always flat. The roughness thresholds are lower than the US map's (85 m and 260 m on 25 km hexes) because a smaller hex spans less relief: they were set so that Spain has the same shares of flat land, hills and mountains as the US rule gives it on 25 km hexes.
notes.cover: From CORINE Land Cover 2018 (Copernicus), sampled on a grid inside each Spanish hex. The CORINE classes are matched to the NLCD-style groups below (the matching table is in CORINE's Almanac entry); water (5xx) and no-data pixels are dropped, the shares are of the remaining land points, and the urban threshold applies to the rounded built-up share (CORINE 111, 112, 121–124 and 133). Foreign hexes (Portugal, France, Andorra, Morocco) have cover 0 (none).
